previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, and a history of bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted for a right lower extremity stump infection. She presented after a visiting nurse noted poor wound healing and purulent discharge. She was hypertensive on admission and started on hydralazine. A PICC line was placed for antibiotic administration. Hyponatremia developed and was corrected with saline. She underwent revision and debridement of the stump due to infection, with intraoperative findings of necrotic tissue. MRSA was identified, and she was treated with ciprofloxacin. Postoperatively, pain was managed with a PCA pump, then transitioned to oral opioids. Physical therapy initiated rehabilitation. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged to an extended care facility with a two-week course of antibiotics, wound care instructions, and follow-up planned in three weeks for suture removal.

___ h/o cocaine/opiate abuse, recent ___ admission for PEA, 
NSTEMI in ___, systolic CHF, DM1 c/b b/l BKA amputations, 
admitted to ICU for DKA now resolved, with klebsiella UTI on

# Diabetic Ketoacidosis/DM1: anion gap on admission which closed 
with insulin and IVF. ___ consulted. Restarted on lantus and 
ISS. Blood sugars reasonably well controlled across duration of 
hospitalization.

# UTI: UCx with Klebsiella, less extensively resistant than 
___ isolates at ___. Current isolates sensitive to 
meropenem. Renal ultrasound showed no evidence of 
pyelonephritis. ID consulted. Treated with meropenem for 3-day 
course for simple cystitis. Blood cultures all negative.

# Hypertensive Urgency: The patient's blood pressure was up to 
190s systolic in the ED and required three doses of IV labetalol 
to bring the BP down to 160s systolic. On arrival to the ICU her 
pressures went down to ___ systolic. BP meds held. Slowly being 
restarted. Currently on Lisinopril 20mg and Metoprolol 75mg po 
bid. Lisinopril increased from 5mg to 20mg. Some concern for 
metoprolol in the setting of potential cocaine use but the 
decision was made to continue this as it was felt that the 
patient is very accustomed to this regimen and reports 
refraining from using cocaine at this time.

# Phantom Limb Pain: Patient reporting ___ bilateral limb pain 
during admission. Of note, her gabapentin had initially been 
held in the setting of altered mental status. Her pain was 
treated with opiates and her gabapentin was restarted. Her pain 
was significantly better controlled towards the time of 
discharge.

# Right BKA stump. The patient's right BKA stump has a small 
area of discharge. Vascular surgery was consulted in the ED and 
felt that the stump did not appear infected. X-ray negative for 
osteomyelitis. Wound care consulted. Patient to follow up with 
vascular 2 weeks after discharge.

# Systolic CHF: EF 40% for several years. The etiology of her 
heart problems are likely a combination of her cocaine use, 
hyperlipidemia, and poorly controlled type 1 DM. Ruled out for 
MI. Continued on aspirin. Beta blocker continued once blood 
pressures were stable.

# Normocytic Anemia: HCT 32.5. Hemodynamically stable. Folate, 
B12, Ferritin withn normal limits. Felt appropriate for further 
outpatient evaluation and management.  

# Altered mental status: Thought to be secondary to combination 
of DKA, opiates, and urinary infection. Resolved with resolution 
of above. Home medications including benzos and opiates were 
restarted once her mental status was felt to be at baseline.

# Insomnia: continued on Ambien.

# GERD: Continued on home PPI.  

# Sacral decubitus ulcer: Wound care consulted and 
recommendations followed.

# Polysubstance abuse. The patient has a history of 
opiate/cocaine abuse in the past. Urine tox screen is positive 
for opiates only which she is prescribed chronically. She denies 
current or recent cocaine use.

radiology_notes.text:
AP AND LATERAL CHEST, ___ AT 1207 HOURS

HISTORY:  Hyperglycemia with elevated white blood cell count.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, the most recent dated ___.

FINDINGS:  Lung volumes are mildly diminished with resultant bronchovascular
crowding.  Subtle cephalization of flow is identified.  There is relatively
streaky opacity now present in the right apical region which was not noted on
the prior exam.  Subtle lingular opacity is also noted projecting over the
heart on frontal view.  The mediastinum is unremarkable.  The cardiac
silhouette is exaggerated by AP technique, however, is at least borderline
enlarged similar to the prior exam.  No effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  An
IVC filter has been previously placed.  The osseous structures are
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  New streaky opacity in the right apical region.  A new infectious
infiltrate cannot be excluded, although the finding is relatively nonspecific.
There is suggestion of central vascular congestion without overt volume
overload.

AP CHEST, 8:11 P.M. ___

HISTORY:  Diabetes, DKA, new left IJ line placement.

IMPRESSION:
AP chest compared to ___:

Tip of the new left internal jugular line projects over the superior
cavoatrial junction.  There is no pneumothorax or mediastinal widening.  ___
be a small left pleural effusion, but in combination with engorgement of upper
lobe vasculature this is more suggestive of mild cardiac decompensation. 
Right upper lobe volume loss is less pronounced, but there is still coarse
peribronchial infiltration.  Overall, these findings suggest recent right
upper lobe aspiration.  Tip of the inferior vena cava umbrella filter projects
over the liver.

COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OF THE THORAX

INDICATION:  Unclear right upper lobe opacity.

COMPARISON:  No comparison available at the time of dictation.

TECHNIQUE:  Volumetric CT acquisitions over the entire thorax in inspiration,
no administration of intravenous contrast material, multiplanar
reconstructions.

FINDINGS:  No supra- or infra-clavicular lymph node enlargement.  However,
numerically increased and borderline-sized lymph nodes are seen in both
axillary regions as well as in the upper mediastinum.  A right central venous
access line is in place.  Moderate coronary calcifications are visualized. 
The size of the heart is at the upper range of normal.  Small hiatal hernia. 
Small bilateral pleural effusions.  Large right subcapsular liver hypodensity
(2A, 47).

The shape of the trachea and the multiple respiratory motion artifacts
indicate that image acquisition was performed during respiration.  As a
consequence, lung volumes are low and the interpretability of the study is
clearly limited.

Mucus is seen in the larger airways (3A, 17).  In the dorsal aspects of the
apical segment of the right upper lobe, a 3.4-cm ill-defined opacity with
central consolidations, air bronchograms, and bronchiectasis is seen.  The
opacity surrounded by several satellite lesions (3A, 21).

In addition, several millimetric parafissural nodules are seen (3A, 24).

Similar but smaller lesions are seen at the bases of the right lower lobe (3A,
38), and at the base of the left lower lobe (3A, 40).

There are no obvious broncho-occlusive lesions, but the right and left main
bronchus show some degree of collapsibility that suggests the potential
presence of tracheobronchomalacia.

There is segmental widening of the esophageal lumen (3A, 16).

The thin sections show mild bronchial wall thickening and bronchial wall
irregularities.

IMPRESSION:  Limited examination due to respiratory motion artifacts. 
Suspicion for increased tracheobronchial collapsibility.  Several partly
ill-defined parenchymal opacities in the periphery of the right upper lobe,
the left lower lobe and the right lower lobe.  The morphology of these
opacities suggests chronic post-infectious changes, supported by areas of
bronchiectasis and small calcifications.  The largest of these lesions is
located in the right upper lobe and is visualized on the chest radiograph.

No evidence for malignancy.

Small pleural effusions.  Moderate coronary calcifications.  Segmental
widening of the esophageal lumen.  Minimal axillary and mediastinal
lymphadenopathy.  Evidence of mild chronic airways disease.

RIGHT KNEE

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Diabetes.  BKA.  Drainage from right stump.

An AP view was obtained which extends past the amputation level.  Lateral view
was obtained, excluding the far distal aspect of the tibia.

Since the study ___, the patient has undergone a BKA at the
proximal diaphyseal level.  On the AP view, the distal ends of the fibula and

IMPRESSION:  No abnormalities are seen at the amputation site that suggest
